figures.caption: Lipid A structure of (A) A. Baumannii, (B) E. coli, and (C) K. pneumonia. E. coli and K. pneumonia primarily contain hexa-acetylated Lipid A, while A. baumannii share much similarity but lipid A is primarily hepta-acetylated. P. aeruginosa differs from the other Gram-negative species in that, its hexa-acetylated Lipid A had a different distribution of Acyl chains and the acyl chains were generally shorter. Numbers below acyl chains indicated the length of the carbon chain. Figures are adapted from Raetz [37], Boll [38], Li [39], and Kim [40].
